title: The Frogs Who Desired a King
text:
The frogs of a quiet pond grew tired of living without a ruler. They sent a delegation to Jupiter and begged him to give them a king. Jupiter, amused by their simplicity, dropped a large log into the water.

The splash sent every frog diving to the bottom in terror. For a long while none dared to look. At last a brave one peeped out and saw that the new king never moved. Soon the frogs swam up to it, climbed onto it, sat on its back and treated it with open contempt. A king who did nothing, they decided, was no king at all, and they went back to Jupiter to demand a real one.

This time Jupiter lost patience. In the version told by the Roman poet Phaedrus he sent them a water snake, and in later retellings a stork. The new ruler was anything but idle. It stalked along the bank and began to seize and eat the frogs one by one. The frogs cried out to Jupiter to take it away, but he refused. They had asked for a king who would act, and now they had one.
lesson: Before you demand a stronger hand in charge, ask what that strength will be used for. A dull but harmless authority can be far better than an energetic and cruel one.
people: The frogs, Jupiter, King Log, King Stork
